datasets_from_scratch_no_english_source.evidence: 6 new tasks are constructed from Bing and MSN data natively sourced in each language without translating from English. Additionally, CoNLL NER, UDPOS, and MLQA are existing datasets with native-language data.

datasets_translated_from_english.evidence: XNLI is translated from English MultiNLI corpus (Conneau et al., 2018). PAWS-X extends English PAWS data to other languages via translation (Yang et al., 2019a).

details.NC: News articles crawled from MSN in each language, reflecting region-specific news topics
details.QADSM: Search queries and ads from Bing in each language, reflecting real user behavior
details.WPR: Web pages and queries from Bing in each language
details.QAM: Question-passage pairs from Bing in each language
details.QG: Passage-question pairs from Bing in each language
details.NTG: News body-title pairs from MSN in each language
details.CoNLL NER: Native-language text from ECI Multilingual Text Corpus

all_annotators_native_speakers.evidence: The paper states labeling was done on 'an Microsoft internal crowdsourcing platform' with guidelines and tests, but does not specify whether annotators are native speakers of each target language.

creator_types_across_datasets: researchers (CoNLL, UD, MLQA, XNLI, PAWS-X original papers)
automated (QG es/it/pt via in-house QA ranker)
annotator_workforce.evidence: For tasks QADSM, WPR, QAM and QG, we label the data on an Microsoft internal crowdsourcing platform. Each labeler must learn the guideline and pass the labeling test. Each sample is labeled by three labeler. We only keep the samples with two or three labeler have same label. For tasks NC and NTG, we directly use the category label on MSN website. All the category label on MSN is review by human.

cultural_flags.english_centricity_notes: The benchmark is inherently English-centric by design: for all 11 tasks, training data is ONLY available in English. Models must learn from English training data and transfer to other languages (zero-shot cross-lingual transfer). 2 of 11 datasets (XNLI, PAWS-X) are direct translations from English. The benchmark explicitly frames cross-lingual evaluation as transferring English-learned skills to other languages.

notably_excluded: Sub-Saharan Africa (except Swahili in XNLI only)
geographic_representation.evidence: 19 languages total. Heavy concentration on European languages (de, es, fr, it, nl, pl, pt, ru, bg, el = 10/19). East/Southeast Asian: zh, vi, th, ja (3-4/19). South Asian: hi, ur (2/19). Middle East: ar (1/19). East Africa: sw (1/19, only in XNLI). No coverage of indigenous, Oceanic, or most African languages.
